title: IMAP all-folder pagination drops results when offset is used
reasoning: search_all_folders computes remaining_budget as limit + offset, but each folder query is capped to min(remaining_budget, limit). With offset=10 and limit=10, a folder with many newest messages contributes only 10 summaries, then the final offset removes them all, so messages 11-20 from that folder are never considered. The per-folder cap should allow collecting enough candidates to satisfy the global offset plus limit.
recommendation: Use remaining_budget, not limit, as the per-folder cap, and consider collecting enough sorted candidates before applying the final global offset.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests are included for search_all_folders with nonzero offset.
suggestedRegressionTest: Mock two selectable folders where the first folder has more than offset + limit messages, call search_all_folders with offset and limit, and assert the returned page contains the expected post-offset messages.
minimumFixScope: Adjust per-folder limit calculation in IMAPReadOnlyConnector.search_all_folders and cover offset pagination.

history.reasoning: The original evidence path still exists in src/imap_readonly_mcp/connectors/imap.py, and search_all_folders now sets per_folder_limit = remaining_budget rather than capping each folder at limit. This allows a single folder to return offset + limit candidates before the final global offset is applied, addressing the reported drop where offset=10/limit=10 previously fetched only 10 and then discarded them. A regression test exists in tests/test_imap_connector.py asserting offset=10/limit=10 returns messages 11-20 from a folder with enough messages.
